title: Bitcoin Core wallet rebroadcast can reveal which node's IP address tracks a Bitcoin address, researcher reports
geo_basis: open-source software issue, no place stated
summary: Bitcoin Core contributor ismaelsadeeq posted research on 25 November showing that wallet rebroadcast of unconfirmed payments can link a Bitcoin address to the IP address of a node whose wallet tracks it. Cyber Security News says it does not allow theft of funds or key recovery. The post says a workaround is -walletbroadcast=0; a proposed change in PR #36482 is unreleased.
plain: A researcher showed that Bitcoin Core's wallet re-announcing of unconfirmed transactions can let an observer tie a Bitcoin address to the IP address of a node that tracks it. It does not expose funds or keys, per Cyber Security News.
exec: A Bitcoin Core wallet privacy leak could tie addresses to node IP addresses; the research post lists a workaround and an unreleased fix proposal.
action: The researcher's post advises setting -walletbroadcast=0 and relaying your own transactions with sendrawtransaction; this also disables wallet-initiated relay generally.

validation.note: The researcher's own post and Cyber Security News, which relays it; one original report. No Bitcoin Core release or advisory was read.

review.note: plain said unpaid transactions; sources say unconfirmed (wording). Rest matches Delving Bitcoin and Cyber Security News
